---
title: "Getting started"
description: "Choose a project, prepare its checkout, and validate the actual revision you will use."
---

import { CodeBlock } from '../../components/ui';

<section className="doc-section">

<h2 id="start-with-a-checkout"><a href="#start-with-a-checkout">Start with a checkout</a></h2>

The source repository is the starting point, not a download button that promises a working runtime on every machine. Read the current README, toolchain requirements, and workspace setup before running project commands.

For ABI, a checkout is a useful first step. The repository may have sibling-workspace or environment requirements, so cloning alone is not a guarantee that a build will succeed.

<CodeBlock code={"git clone https://github.com/donaldfilimon/abi.git\ncd abi"} />

</section>

<section className="doc-section">

<h2 id="use-the-project-wrapper"><a href="#use-the-project-wrapper">Use the project wrapper</a></h2>

ABI documents a nightly Rust workflow through its tools/cargo.sh wrapper. Use the wrapper rather than substituting a different local Cargo toolchain. Its check script is the primary validation gate described by the README.

<CodeBlock code={"./tools/cargo.sh --version\n./tools/check.sh\n./tools/cargo.sh build -p abi-cli"} note={"Documentation commands, not executed results. Prepare the upstream toolchain and workspace first."} />

</section>

<section className="doc-section">

<h2 id="inspect-before-connecting"><a href="#inspect-before-connecting">Inspect before connecting</a></h2>

Once your own build succeeds, the README describes local inspection commands for available backends and scheduler state. A backend name is not proof that hardware acceleration is active. Read the capability flags and their limitations.

<CodeBlock code={"./target/debug/abi backends\n./target/debug/abi scheduler status"} />

</section>

<section className="doc-section">

<h2 id="keep-checks-scoped"><a href="#keep-checks-scoped">Keep checks scoped</a></h2>

Record the revision, machine, toolchain, command, and result when you verify a behavior. A passing local build does not establish production latency, cross-host behavior, or another platform’s acceptance.

Gama and the existing MLAI website have their own build instructions. Do not run ABI commands inside those projects. This preview neither creates credentials nor starts a live provider connection.

</section>
